# 231 — PR explainer

## Goal

The daily audit's `occlusion` lens visits 83 surfaces a tick and reports how many are covered by a
fixed overlay. On 2026-08-04, item 221's verifier established what that report is actually worth:
against the `dead-pool` surface — a page measured to be **permanently** broken (a manual probe
mirroring the lens's own sequence caught the occluded geometry on ~14 of 14 runs, never once clean;
item 230 then reproduced it 10 of 10 with an independent instrument) — the lens flagged it on
**3 of 20** isolated runs. **15%.**

That number is not a cosmetic problem. The *fixed-overlay-occlusion* class has produced six items
(179 → 217 → 218 → 220 → 221 → 230), and LEARNINGS' standing rule is that a filter returning zero is
not evidence of health until it has been shown able to return non-zero. A lens with a 15% hit rate
makes every "0 blocking findings" tick a far stronger claim than its evidence supports — RAZOR side 1,
on the loop's own instrument.

This item's deliverable is therefore **a number, not a pixel**: the detection rate itself.

## The intuition

`checkOcclusion()` resized the page to 780px tall, slept a flat 150 ms, and measured. Both halves of
that are assumptions wearing a timer:

- **the resize might not have landed.** Every occlusion this lens exists to catch is height-dependent
  by construction — `OCCLUSION_HEIGHT = 780` is precisely the height at which item 218's defect
  appears, and at the 900px the surfaces render at, the same bottom-fixed footer clears the same
  victims. `occlusionPassEval` reads `window.innerHeight` directly. Measure before the renderer
  applies the resize and you measure the *old* viewport, where the footer intersects nothing: a clean
  result that is a false negative by construction.
- **the page might not be finished.** A React surface re-renders on resize. 150 ms is a guess about
  when that ends.

So: stop guessing, and never let an unverified read count as clean.

## What changed, and why — in reading order

`audit-app.js`, inside `checkOcclusion()` only. **Zero product-file diff.**

**1. Assert the viewport instead of assuming it.** After `setViewportSize`, poll (bounded 2000 ms, via
the file's existing `pollFor`) until `window.innerWidth`/`innerHeight` actually equal the target. If
they never do, push a **P2** naming the measured values and **skip both passes**. A measurement at
the wrong viewport is a lie, not a clean — and this lens's standing doctrine is that a check must
never fail silently.

**2. Wait for a quiet dwell — observe, don't sample.** This is the part attempt 1 got wrong, and the
correction is the interesting half of the item.

Attempt 1 replaced the flat sleep with a *convergence poll*: sample a layout signature until two
consecutive samples ≥100 ms apart are identical, then measure. It scored **20/20** on its fixture and
passed all nine literal acceptance criteria. The verifier failed it anyway, by building the fixture
attempt 1's own design notes had ruled out: a page that is **quiescent for >100 ms and then makes one
instantaneous late change**. Measured detection: **0 of 10**, at every quiet interval tried — reported
clean, with no advisory, because from the poll's point of view convergence genuinely held. A sampling
rule is satisfied by a page that merely happens to be still at the moment you look.

The fix is to stop sampling for stillness and **observe change**: a `MutationObserver`
(childList + subtree + attributes + characterData) plus a `ResizeObserver` on `documentElement` and on
every visible fixed/sticky element — the exact overlay set the lens's verdict depends on. Wait until
`QUIET_MS = 150` elapses with **no observed change**; every change **re-arms** the dwell; the whole
wait is capped at `BUDGET_MS` (shipped at 1500 — see "Why this is PARKED" for why that number is the
whole story). Budget exhausted while still churning → P2 advisory **and measure anyway** (a positive
on an unsettled page is still evidence; its absence is not).

**3. A floor, and the impossibility behind it.** The revised spec asked
for the dwell alone. Built exactly that way, it measured **7/20** on the single-late-change family —
tied with the pre-fix control, no improvement at all. The reason is not a bug: **a `setTimeout` that
has not fired yet is unobservable to every DOM API.** No observer can re-arm on a change that has not
happened. Against a change scheduled at an unknown future time, the only defense is a horizon. So the dwell also carries a
floor.

Attempt 2 anchored that floor to **page navigation** (`MIN_PAGE_AGE_MS = 500`) and the verifier killed
it: real dwell-start page ages span **196 ms** (`landing`) to **~13,000 ms** (`static-page`), so the
floor was neither the no-op the notes claimed nor uniformly protective — on the old-page side the
mechanism decayed to the QUIET_MS-only design, measured at **8/20**. Attempt 3 anchors every term to
**dwell start** instead: watch until `max(MIN_WATCH_MS, last observed change + QUIET_MS)`, capped at
`BUDGET_MS`. **Page age is not an input.** That is what makes the three fixture families agree.

## The numbers

| | measured |
|---|---|
| Pre-fix, motivating instance (`dead-pool`, item 221) | **3/20 (15%)** |
| Continuously-settling fixture — pre-fix control / shipped | 7/20 → **20/20** |
| Single instantaneous late change — attempt 1 / shipped | **0/10** → **20/20** |
| Same, on a page already old at dwell start — attempt 2 / shipped | **8/20** → **20/20** |
| Real product surfaces, settled reference probe — before → after | `grid-token` 1/7 → **7/7**, `grid-chain` 2/7 → **7/7**, `grid-768` 6/7 → **7/7**, `grid-360` 7/7 → 7/7 |

The last row is the one that matters, because it is the only one measured on the real product: two
grid surfaces that read as *intermittently* broken were reliably broken all along, and the lens was
the intermittent part. That is item 231's whole thesis, confirmed — and it retires a question backlog
row 233 would otherwise have had to ask.

Non-vacuity, both rules neutered **separately** against the shipped file (byte-identical restore
proven by `md5sum` each time): removing the viewport assertion → RED; replacing the dwell with the old
flat 150 ms sleep → RED, failing criteria 1b **and** 1d specifically. Neither rule is decorative.

## Why this is PARKED and not merged

The mechanism works. The budget does not allow it, and the two gates that disagree are both this
item's own.

`BUDGET_MS` — the cap on how long the dwell may wait — is squeezed from both sides:

- **From below:** `pool-detail`'s own `AnimatedNumber` churn settles at **750–1191 ms** (15+ samples).
  Cap the dwell under that and the pass measures a still-animating page, producing **4 false P2
  occlusion findings on `pool-detail*`** — the one surface class `test_audit_app.js` declares *never
  eligible for quarantine*, because it is 217's and 218's regression rail. So `BUDGET_MS ≳ 1200–1300`.
- **From above:** a real `runAudit({poolLiveness:false})` leg must stay inside +20%. So
  `BUDGET_MS ≲ 950–1000`.

Measured, two runs each, base `adf6d6dc21` via `git worktree`:

| `BUDGET_MS` | real leg | pool-detail rail |
|---|---|---|
| 2000 (attempt 2) | +23.4% | pass |
| 900 | **+19.01%** (18.79 / 19.24) | **FAILS** — 4 false P2s |
| 1500 | +27.34% (26.27 / 28.42) — 238.68 s → ~304 s | pass |

**The windows do not overlap.** That is a measured structural result, not an unfinished search.

And one number turns "slower" into a real cost: `FOREGROUND_CAP_MS = 300 s` (`audit-app.js:268`) is
`DEFAULT_TIME_BUDGET_MS`, and past it `runAudit`'s render loop **skips pool surfaces**. At ~304 s this
fix would quietly buy detection reliability with audit *coverage*. A loop should not make that trade
without being asked.

## The one question for the human

**May the daily audit take ~305 s instead of ~239 s?** Any one of these ships this branch unchanged:
raise `FOREGROUND_CAP_MS` above 300 s; move the audit off the foreground path; or shrink the surface
population to pay for the dwell.

A **no** is just as actionable: then the right item is not this one but a cheaper detector — for
example, re-measuring only the surfaces observed to churn — and this branch is the evidence for why
that is the shape to build.

## The limit, stated plainly

The lens sees any DOM- or resize-observable change inside
`max(MIN_WATCH_MS, last observed change + QUIET_MS)` from dwell start, capped at `BUDGET_MS`. An
occlusion first appearing after that horizon is outside its reach by construction — you cannot detect
an arbitrarily late change without watching arbitrarily long, and watching 83 surfaces arbitrarily
long is precisely the cost this item parked on. The hunt for a surviving shape found one: a pure CSS
**`transform`** change (no resize, no DOM mutation) landing after `MIN_WATCH_MS` still evades it. No
product occlusion of that shape is known today.

This item claims exactly one thing, and it is checkable: **the lens's timing-induced false negatives
are fixed, within a stated horizon, at a cost the audit's current budget cannot absorb.**

## Class left open, with numbers

`grep -n "waitForTimeout(" audit-app.js` finds 4 sites. `:3464` is `pollFor`'s poll interval, not a
measurement gate; `:4202` is what this item replaced; `:4253` is pass 2's settle, already guarded by a
`scrollHeight`-stability condition. The survivor is **`:3613`** — a flat 400 ms sleep in the
`static`-kind driver, immediately before `auditText()`, gating the text/number audit of **every static
surface**, the bulk of the 83. Its false-negative rate has never been measured; this item did not
measure it and does not claim to. Filed as **BACKLOG 232**. The newly-solid grid findings — including
`grid-768`, which is occluded and quarantined nowhere — are **BACKLOG 233**.

## Quiz (HIGH tier)

1. The lens scored 3/20 on a page proven broken ~14/14 by hand. Why does a *low* detection rate make
   the daily "0 blocking findings" report actively misleading rather than merely incomplete?
2. Attempt 1's convergence poll passed all nine of its acceptance criteria at 20/20 and was still
   failed. What exactly did its predicate — "two consecutive identical samples" — fail to distinguish?
3. Attempt 2 replaced sampling with observers and *still* failed. What was wrong with anchoring its
   floor to page navigation, given that real dwell-start page ages run from 196 ms to ~13,000 ms?
4. Why can no observer, however well written, catch a change scheduled by a `setTimeout` that has not
   fired yet — and what is the only defense against it?
5. `BUDGET_MS=900` costs +19.01% and passes the cost gate. Why is shipping it the *worst* of the three
   options on the table?
